answer: Proof-of-burn mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to permanently destroy cryptocurrency at unspendable addresses to register an identity. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of forfeiting financial capital per identity, rooted like durable cedar rather than spawned as costless bots. Peers verify burn proofs with the vigilance of a falcon as reputation scales toward a voting summit. A key limitation is plutocratic bias, allowing wealthy adversaries to buy disproportionate influence.
